$comment: Canonical HMAC request-signing vectors, shared by the Python and TypeScript
The scheme exists in two languages: src/tradelens/api/security.py signs and
verifies on the backend, web/lib/api/sign.ts signs on the Vercel side. They
cannot import each other, so these vectors are what stops them drifting into
two subtly different schemes that agree in each suite and disagree in
production. Follows the precedent of auth-contract-vectors.json.
The query is CANONICALISED before signing: every name and value is RFC 3986
percent-encoded (unreserved set is A-Za-z0-9 and -._~), then pairs are sorted
by encoded name and then encoded value. Raw signing would mean ?a=1&b=2 and
?b=2&a=1 produced different signatures for the same request.

vectors.name: GET with an empty body and no query
non-ASCII body is UTF-8 encoded before hashing
a simple query is bound into the signature
query parameter order does not change the signature
repeated keys are sorted by value, both retained
blank values are kept, not dropped
plus and percent-20 both mean space and canonicalise alike
non-ASCII query values are percent-encoded consistently
sub-delims are escaped rather than left bare
